slides.text: The Linlithgow offer The August Offer was an offer made by Viceroy Linlithgow in 1940 promising the expansion of the chief Council of the Viceroy of India to incorporate more Indians, the establishment of an advisory war council, giving full weight to the minority opinion, and therefore the recognition of Indians ' righ t to border their constitution after the top of the war . In return, it had been hoped that each one part y and communities in India would cooperate in Britain ' s efforts in World War II. However , this proposal was rejected by Congress because the minorities, especially the Muslim League, were assured that no constitutional scheme was acceptable to the govt without their agreement , i.e. providing a veto power to the Muslim League.
